N-Zero — Smarter Carbon Manager

Sole product designer · Onboarding, emissions calculator and carbon offset planner
ClientN-Zero, Sydney
SectorCarbon markets & ESG
RoleSole designer, end to end
ToolsFigma
The client

Carbon credits, made implementable.

N-Zero is a Sydney company building what it calls a smarter carbon manager — an AI and blockchain powered digital carbon markets advisor, manager and ESG reporting platform. Its premise is that most businesses now accept they need to act on emissions but have no practical route from intent to action: carbon credits are opaque, hard to evaluate, and easy to get wrong.

The platform’s stated job is to make carbon credits simple, safe and implementable, through tailored advice, actionable strategies and impact-focused ESG reports. Four things sit underneath that:

Pillar 01

Tailored carbon advice

An AI advisor assesses the company’s climate goals and recommends compliance and voluntary carbon credits that fit its strategy.

Pillar 02

ESG dashboards & reports

Verified co-benefits tracked and reported — air quality, biodiversity protection of native vegetation, soil resilience.

Pillar 03

Buy, sell and retire credits

A trading platform with trades, order books, bids and asks reported in real time.

Pillar 04

Quality scorecard

Credits scored against additionality, non-overestimation, permanence, non double counting and no harm — a guard against greenwashing.

The design problem

Two users in one seat.

N-Zero describes its flow in five steps: register, climate goals assessment, carbon credit portfolio analysis, climate advice and action, then monitor and manage. My work covered the middle of that — everything between a company signing up and holding a costed offset plan.

The difficulty is that those steps serve two different people. Establishing a baseline is operational work: someone who knows how many containers move through a port each year. Choosing and buying credits is financial and strategic work: someone thinking about budget, timeframe and disclosure. The platform had to carry one person from the first job to the second without the interface feeling like two products bolted together.

Brand

Forest green on near-black.

N-Zero’s identity is a dot-matrix wordmark and a deep forest green — not the bright mint most carbon platforms reach for. The navigation runs near-black, warming into dark green at the foot of the rail, so the sidebar reads as a surface rather than a slab. Inside the calculator the green does one job and does it consistently: filled green means a stage you have finished, mint means the stage you are on, grey means a stage you have not reached. The tab bar is a progress meter that happens to be navigation.

Working prototype

The report builds itself.

Thirteen screens, and you drive them. The real buttons are live — Login now, Next, the calculator tabs, every stage in the bar — so the path from sign-in to a carbon credit portfolio is walked rather than described. Click anywhere else to flash every hotspot on the screen. Nothing is wired to a backend, so every figure is sample data.

The thing worth noticing is that there is no “generate report” moment. The report is assembled from the work the user has already done: six stages of logistics data become a footprint, the footprint and the offset goal become a shortlist of sequestration options, the chosen options become a purchase plan and a credit portfolio. Export report at the end is a formality, not a step.

Every screen here is exported from the Figma file at full resolution, in the product’s own colours, so this runs without Figma and without a network call. Year wise Plan is the one tab not wired up; it says so when clicked.

Stage 01–05

Each leg of the supply chain takes its own inputs — containers offloaded per year and average weight per container, split across TEU and FEU at the port — and reports its own emissions beside a cumulative subtotal that carries forward.

Stage 06

The summary closes the calculator at 28,754.5 kg CO₂e and hands that total, plus the offset goal and timeframe, to the planner.

Recommendations

Options are compared on capacity, CO₂ offset per year, average life and cost per unit — solar rooftop at 9,900 kg/yr over 20 years, tree plantation at 3,000 kg/yr over 40 — so the choice weighs longevity against price, not price alone.

Credits & portfolio

Real registry projects, filterable by method and location — savanna fire management and native forest regeneration across the Northern Territory and Western Australia — resolving into portfolio value, emission offset and balance remaining.

Baseline

Follow the goods, not the form.

N-Zero’s assessment step needs emission scopes and baselines before it can recommend anything. For an importer, that baseline lives in the supply chain — so instead of one long emissions form, the calculator walks the physical journey of the goods and asks about one leg at a time.

01

At Port

Containers offloaded per year, by TEU and FEU, with weight per container.

02

Transit

Road and rail movement from port inland.

03

At Warehouse

Storage, handling and facility emissions.

04

Transfer

Movement into the distribution network.

05

Dist. Warehouse

Final-leg storage and distribution.

06

Summary

Totals by process and by GHG scope.

Each stage shows its own result and a cumulative sub-total, so the number grows as the user works instead of appearing only at the end. The summary then splits the same total two ways: by process, for the operations side, and by Scope 1, 2 and 3, because that is the shape an ESG disclosure has to take. Neither group has to do the translation.

Design decisions

Four calls worth explaining.

Journey as navigation

Structuring the calculator around the path of the goods, rather than around emission categories, let users answer from operational knowledge they already had.

Goal captured at sign-up

Offset target and timeframe are asked for during onboarding, so every later recommendation is measured against a number the company chose rather than presented as an open menu.

Two readings of one total

Process and scope views side by side, serving the operations team and the reporting team from the same calculation.

Options costed, not listed

Sequestration choices show capacity, annual CO₂ offset, average life and offset per unit, so the planner compares on effect and longevity instead of price alone.
